SddDiagramVocabulary.keywords: diagram selection, mermaid, ascii, spec diagrams, overview, vision, use cases, data flow, architecture, sequence, state, er, sdd-diagram-vocabulary
SddDiagramVocabulary.Mission:
Diagram-selection cheat sheet for SDD v2 authoring, ported from the field-tested `messenger` `visual-vocabulary.xml` and adapted to gennady's structure: gennady does NOT carry a separate `## Диаграммы` section — the mandatory diagram lives directly inside `## Overview` (checked by `SDD_NO_DIAGRAM_BLOCK` / `SDD_DIAGRAM_BLOCK_EMPTY`, `shared/sdd/check.ts`). This file is the shared reference the five `formats/*-spec-structure.xml` templates and `interview-protocol.directive.xml` point to instead of each re-deriving the same table.
Two destinations, one vocabulary: - **Chat** (interview, decision cards): ASCII / emoji only — mermaid does NOT render in chat. Drawn BEFORE the decision is made, so the operator judges the shape, not the wording. - **Spec** (`## Overview`, plus inline wherever another section's meaning is relational): mermaid. `Overview`'s diagram is never folded (it is the human-readable top half); a diagram added deeper in a folded section rides inside that section's ``.
Loaded by `interview-protocol.directive.xml` (chat forms) and by the five `formats/*-spec-structure.xml` templates (Overview diagram + any additional diagram by author judgment). The mechanical checks verify only PRESENCE/non-emptiness of the Overview diagram block; the ≤7-node and one-idea-per-diagram rules are judgment calls made at write time, not re-derived by a tool.
The module flow's diagram FLOOR (not judgment — see `AX_SPEC_MANDATORY_DIAGRAM` in `module.directive.xml`) is beyond a single Overview picture: a fixed ladder of one diagram per decomposition step (Module Map axes, Entity Inventory ER, Entity Surface lifecycle, Module Contracts dependency graph, Call Chain sequence — new per the 2026-08-20 visualization-chain decision), plus a Delta rung (composition graph with the new node marked, added Call Chain steps) whenever the module is under `refine`/`pivot`. The full worked example, ASCII + mermaid pair per rung, lives at `ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-diagram-ladder.example.md` — each of `module.directive.xml`'s `STEP_1_MODULE_MAP` … `STEP_4_CONTRACTS_DBC` / `STEP_6_FINAL_HIERARCHY` points to it directly. The scope flow carries its own analogous floor — Overview, High-Level Architecture, Use Cases (`product` only), Data Flow (`product`/`library`, drawn AFTER requirements close) — see `AX_SPEC_MANDATORY_DIAGRAM` in `scope.directive.xml`.

BeliefState.Axiom: Relational meaning → picture; a single judgement (one entity, one scalar choice) stays text — a diagram of one node is noise. The rule is not "always draw"; it is "if the thing to understand is a relationship among ≥2 elements positioned in space, a picture beats a paragraph".

Every diagram, any medium: ≤7 nodes (split or abstract if more); ONE diagram per idea; a one-line caption directly under it (Russian, per `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE` — the caption is operator-facing text), in the exact shape `DIAGRAM_CAPTION_FORMAT` fixes below; encode the single thing to notice first with position/size/marker. A diagram nobody reads in 5 seconds failed — simplify.

Every scope and module spec's `## Overview` carries ≥1 diagram — this is the mechanical floor (`SDD_NO_DIAGRAM_BLOCK` / `SDD_DIAGRAM_BLOCK_EMPTY`). The floor picture is the one that answers "what is this, at a glance": system-context for a scope, main happy-path flow for a module. Add more diagrams elsewhere in the spec by judgment whenever a second view genuinely helps a reader (sequence, data-flow, state, before/after for a pivot) — never as decoration.

A spec diagram is not born at write-time: during the interview the same relation is shown in chat as ASCII at the step boundary where the decision is made (per `interview-protocol` `AX_VISUAL_WHEN_RELATIONAL`). Write-time only converts the already-agreed shape to mermaid — a diagram appearing for the first time in the final spec means the operator never saw the shape they approved.

SddDiagramVocabulary.DiagramSelection:
Pick the row by INTENT (left). All core types have a clean ASCII form for chat AND a mermaid form for the spec.
| Intent — what you show | Diagram | Chat form (ASCII) | Spec form (mermaid) | |---|---|---|---| | Scope's place among neighbours / system boundary | C4-style | boxes grouped in a boundary zone | `flowchart` + `subgraph` | | Business goals → scenarios (who comes and why) | use-case | actors → scenario nodes, one line each | `flowchart` TD | | Where data came from, where it turned into what, where it landed (scope-level Data Flow rung) | DFD | four node kinds only — entity/process/store/labelled arrow, NO branches or loops | `flowchart` (DFD-restricted — see `Syntax` below) | | Dependencies / coupling / direction (module Overview, Module Contracts) | flowchart | boxes + arrows | `flowchart` LR | | Who calls whom over time (module Call Chain rung) | sequence | participant columns + arrows (≤4 cols); table-of-steps is an equally valid form for a linear scenario | `sequenceDiagram` (or a Step/Participant/Action/Data table) | | Lifecycle / statuses (state machine in the design) | state | `A -> B` labelled transitions | `stateDiagram-v2` | | Point of a PIVOT / refine (old shape vs new, module Delta rung) | before→after | composition graph with the new node marked `NEW` | `flowchart` with `:::new` on the added node, or a `(добавлено)` suffix | | Data schema (entities / tables) | ER | indented entity→fields list | `erDiagram` | | File map / hierarchy | tree | indented ASCII tree | (plain fenced text — `## File Structure` already uses this) |
Niche mermaid types (pie, gantt, timeline, journey, mindmap, gitGraph, quadrantChart, …) — skip for SDD specs: no clean ASCII twin for chat, rarely earn their place in a spec.
SddDiagramVocabulary.Syntax:
Minimal skeletons; keep ≤7 nodes. ASCII = chat, mermaid = spec.
ASCII: ┌─ Boundary: Session ──────────────────┐ │ [Middleware] ──▶ [Store iface] │ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┴──────┐ │ │ ▼ ▼ │ │ [MemoryStore] [RedisStore 🆕] │ └───────────────────────────────────────┘ Mermaid: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Session MW[Middleware] --> IF[Store iface] IF --> MEM[MemoryStore] IF --> RDS[RedisStore] end ```
ASCII: [caller] ──request──▶ [Port] ──▶ [Service] ──result──▶ [caller] Mermaid: ```mermaid flowchart LR caller -->|request| Port Port --> Service Service -->|result| caller ```
Exactly four node kinds, NO conditions, NO loops — this is a data diagram, not a control-flow chart; a branch belongs on a state/flowchart elsewhere, never here. ASCII: (user) ──submits──▶ [validate & save] ──row──▶ ((tasks store)) │ confirmation ▼ (user) Mermaid — external entity = rounded `(...)`, process = rectangle `[...]`, store = cylinder `[(...)]`, flow = a labelled arrow, nothing else: ```mermaid flowchart LR user(user) -->|submits task| validate[validate & save] validate -->|row| store[(tasks store)] validate -->|confirmation| user ```
ASCII (columns, ≤4 participants): Client API DB │ POST │ │ │─────────▶│ query │ │ │─────────▶│ │ │◀─────────│ │◀─────────│ │ Mermaid: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram Client->>API: POST API->>DB: query DB-->>API: rows API-->>Client: 201 ``` Table-of-steps — an equally valid form for a linear scenario, no diagram penalty for choosing it (`CALL_CHAIN_FORMAT`, `formats/dbc-contracts.xml`): | Step | Participant | Action | Data | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Client | POST /orders | order payload | | 2 | API | query DB | order id | | 3 | DB | return rows | order row | | 4 | API | 201 to Client | order id |
ASCII: [draft] ──open──▶ [review] ──approve──▶ [merged] │ reject ──▶ [closed] Mermaid: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 draft --> review: open review --> merged: approve review --> closed: reject ```
ASCII: User ──1:N──▶ Session - id (PK) - id (PK) - email - user_id (FK) Mermaid: ```mermaid erDiagram USER ||--o{ SESSION : has ```

Output_Contracts.Contract:
Decided 2026-08-20 (`specs/ai-skills/research/2026-08-20-visualization-chain.research.md`) — fixes the exact caption shape every diagram in a spec carries, mermaid or (chat-only) ASCII; this is what a mechanical grep traces a diagram back to its requirements with, so the shape below is normative and MUST NOT drift. Directly after the closing fence, one line:
```markdown ```mermaid ... ``` _<Что показывает одной фразой> — -REQ-[, -REQ-]._ ```
Example: `_Путь данных при добавлении задачи — STOR-REQ-3, STOR-REQ-7._`
The ID list names the requirements THIS diagram shows — not every requirement in the spec, and never a requirement the diagram does not actually depict. A diagram that illustrates no single requirement (a whole-system Overview, a scope-boundary picture among neighbours) drops the ID list but keeps the phrase — `_Как сцеплен с соседями._` — the caption itself has no exception, only the ID suffix is conditional. MANDATORY for every diagram in every spec; held mechanically by the check `sdd-check` gates for this shape.

The Overview diagram sits directly in `## Overview` — NOT wrapped in `` (it is the human-readable floor of the spec's top half). Fenced mermaid (spec) — never ASCII in the final spec text; ASCII is the chat-only intermediate. Caption directly under the fence per `DIAGRAM_CAPTION_FORMAT` — Overview is whole-scope, so the no-ID form applies by default.
```markdown
## Overview
```mermaid flowchart LR caller -->|request| Port Port --> Service Service -->|result| caller ``` _Что здесь главное, одной фразой._
```
Additional diagrams elsewhere in the spec follow the same fenced-mermaid-plus-caption shape (caption per `DIAGRAM_CAPTION_FORMAT`, ID list included whenever the diagram shows specific requirements); when placed inside a section already required to fold (`FOLD_REQUIRED_V2`, `shared/sdd/check.ts`), the diagram rides inside that section's `` like the rest of the reference detail.
